category: Identify appropriate diagnostic investigations, especially imaging
front: Q: Identify the four clinical predictors used to differentiate pediatric septic arthritis from transient synovitis.
back:
1. History of fever >38.5°C.
2. Non-weight-bearing.
3. ESR >40 mm/h.
4. White cell count >12 × 10⁹/L.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [The clinical predictors of Kocher et al. (2004) for the diagnosis of septic arthritis: History of fever >38.5°C, Non-weight-bearing, Erythrocyte sedimentation rate >40 mm/h, White cell count >12 × 10 9 /L.]

category: Identify appropriate diagnostic investigations, especially imaging
front: Q: Contrast the diagnostic timing and sensitivity of plain radiographs versus MRI in acute osteomyelitis.
back:
* MRI: Preferred; shows edema and periosteal elevation within 2–3 days.
* Radiographs: Often normal for up to 1 week; later show osteopenia or periosteal reaction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 603 (Book Page): [In the early phase (2–3 days) radiographs may be normal but MRI will show bone oedema and periosteal elevation. After 5–7 days, plain radiographs may show subtle abnormality with osteopenia and periosteal new bone formation.]

category: Identify appropriate diagnostic investigations, especially imaging
front: Q: Which chest radiographic sign suggests aortic disruption, and what investigation is used for confirmation?
back:
* Sign: Widened mediastinum.
* Confirmation: Contrast CT scan of the mediastinum.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [Erect chest radiography can also suggest thoracic aortic disruption, the most common radiological fnding being a widened mediastinum... The diagnosis is confrmed by a CT scan of the mediastinum.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What criteria must a patient with a mild head injury meet for safe hospital discharge?
back:
- GCS score of 15/15 with no focal deficits.
- Not under the infuence of alcohol/drugs.
- Accompanied by a responsible adult.
- Provision of verbal and written head injury advice.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 383 (Book Page): [UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence discharge criteria in minor and mild head injury... GCS 15/15 with no focal defcits... Patient not under the infuence of alcohol or drugs... Patient accompanied by a responsible adult... Verbal and written head injury advice]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Which specific warning signs necessitate urgent re-evaluation for a head-injured patient following discharge?
back:
- Persistent/worsening headache despite analgesia.
- Persistent vomiting or drowsiness.
- Visual disturbances.
- New limb weakness or numbness.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 383 (Book Page): [seek medical attention if: Persistent/worsening headache despite analgesia; Persistent vomiting; Drowsiness; Visual disturbance; Limb weakness or numbness]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: How should attendants identify the clinical hallmark of early Compartment Syndrome in an injured extremity?
back:
- Pain that is out of proportion to the injury.
- Increasing severity of pain over time.
- Intense pain elicited by passive stretch of the affected muscles.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [Compartment syndrome is a clinical diagnosis characterised by pain out of proportion, increasing pain, and pain on passive stretch, with paraesthesia possible.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What are the mandatory maintenance instructions for the Foot Abduction Orthosis (FAO) in club foot management?
back:
- Worn full-time for the first 3 months post-correction.
- Worn at night and during 'nap time' for up to 4 years.
- Strict compliance is essential to avoid deformity relapse.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 626 (Book Page): [The FAO is worn full time for 3 months and at ‘night and nap time’ for up to 4 years. Poor compliance with the FAO is associated with a higher relapse rate.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What complications should attendants monitor for in an infant wearing a Pavlik harness for hip dysplasia?
back:
- Skin breakdown in skin folds.
- Femoral nerve palsy (demonstrated by loss of active knee extension).
- Avascular necrosis of the femoral head from extreme positioning.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 617 (Book Page): [Most harnesses allow controlled movement while splints hold the hips more rigidly and may carry a greater risk of AVN and femoral nerve palsy.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: How must pressure sores be prevented in insensate patients following a traumatic spinal injury?
back:
- Rapid removal from spinal boards after transfer.
- Regular turning on an appropriate mattress.
- Constant vigilance of the skin envelope in anaesthetic areas.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 390 (Book Page): [Spinal boards lead to skin breakdown in insensate patients... They should only be used for transferring patients... Patients should be turned regularly on an appropriate mattress to minimise the risk of skin breakdown.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What critical documentation is required when a tourniquet is applied for catastrophic external hemorrhage?
back: The exact length of time for which the tourniquet has been applied must be recorded on the patient to prevent irreversible limb ischaemia.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [It is vital to appreciate that once a tourniquet is applied the limb becomes ischaemic; therefore, the length of time for which the tourniquet is applied must be recorded on the patient]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Which modifiable host factors must be addressed to improve outcomes in chronic osteomyelitis?
back:
- Smoking cessation.
- Optimization of diabetes (glycaemic control).
- Management of peripheral vascular disease.
- Nutritional optimization.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 605 (Book Page): [In chronic infection, it is essential to address medical conditions that may impair wound healing (e.g. smoking, peripheral vascular disease, diabetes, steroid use) prior to surgery. This approach has been shown to improve cure rates.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Why is prolonged orthopaedic follow-up required for children surviving neonatal bone and joint sepsis?
back: To monitor for late sequelae such as chronic infection, physeal (growth plate) damage, and secondary joint deformities that manifest during growth.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 636 (Book Page): [signifcant complications can occur... where there has been damage to the joint and/or the physis... Orthopaedic follow-up should be continued until normal growth patterns are documented.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What typical features of concussion should be explained to patients for their post-injury follow-up?
back:
- Persistent headaches and somnolence.
- Amnesia and confusion.
- Irritability or emotional lability.
- Follow-up by a specialist nurse is desirable.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 383 (Book Page): [Many of these patients will struggle with features of concussion for a period after their injury, with headaches and somnolence typical. Follow-up by a head injury specialist nurse or equivalent is therefore desirable.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Which specific symptoms require a head-injured patient to seek immediate medical re-evaluation after discharge?
back:
• Persistent/worsening headache despite analgesia.
• Persistent vomiting.
• Drowsiness or visual disturbance.
• Limb weakness or numbness.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 383 (Book Page): [seek medical attention if: Persistent/worsening headache despite analgesia, Persistent vomiting, Drowsiness, Visual disturbance, Limb weakness or numbness]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What cognitive and somatic disturbances should attendants be educated on regarding postconcussive syndrome?
back:
• Somatic: Headache, dizziness, hearing/vision disorders.
• Cognitive: Poor concentration, recall difficulty, insomnia.
• Emotional: Lability, fatigue, depression.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 383 (Book Page): [Postconcussive syndrome is a loosely defned constellation of symptoms... somatic features such as headache, dizziness... neurocognitive and neuropsychological disturbances, including difculty with concentration and recall]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Contrast the treatment burden for parents of neonates versus toddlers diagnosed with DDH.
back:
• Neonates (<6 months): Non-invasive Pavlik harness or splints.
• Toddlers/Late: Closed or open surgical reduction and spica casting.
• Follow-up: Critical because acetabular remodelling potential drops after age 4.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 618 (Book Page): [Up to age 4–6 months, a harness or splint is efective treatment... The potential for acetabular remodelling decreases after the age of 3–4 years]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: When monitoring a casted limb, which 'red flag' complication symptoms must the attendant report immediately?
back:
• Pain out of proportion to the injury.
• Increasing pain despite analgesia.
• Pain during passive stretch of digits.
• New numbness or paresthesia.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [Compartment syndrome is a clinical diagnosis characterised by pain out of proportion, increasing pain, and pain on passive stretch, with paraesthesia possible.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What is the mandatory long-term follow-up schedule for the Foot Abduction Orthosis (FAO) in clubfoot?
back:
• Initial: Full-time use for 3 months.
• Maintenance: Night and nap-time use until age 4 years.
• Purpose: Essential to prevent high relapse rates.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 626 (Book Page): [The FAO is worn full time for 3 months and at ‘night and nap time’ for up to 4 years. Poor compliance with the FAO is associated with a higher relapse rate.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What specific infection prophylaxis follow-up is mandatory after a trauma-related splenectomy?
back:
• Inoculation: Pneumococcus vaccine.
• Timing: 2–3 weeks post-surgery.
• Goal: Protects against overwhelming post-splenectomy sepsis after immune recovery.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 402 (Book Page): [Inoculation against Pneumococcus is advisable within 2–3 weeks, by which time the patient’s immune system has recovered.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Why is a long-term CT follow-up mandatory for patients recovering from frontal sinus fractures?
back:
• Schedule: CT at 6 months and 1 year post-injury.
• Purpose: To monitor for delayed complications like meningitis, mucoceles, or Pott’s puffy tumour.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 414 (Book Page): [A CT scan at 6 months to 1 year is recommended to ensure that there are no signs of complications.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Which four clinical predictors help attendants distinguish pediatric septic arthritis from transient synovitis?
back:
• History of fever >38.5°C.
• Inability to bear weight.
• Elevated ESR (>40 mm/h).
• Elevated WBC count (>12 × 10^9/L).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 634 (Book Page): [The clinical predictors of Kocher et al. (2004) for the diagnosis of septic arthritis: History of fever >38.5°C, Non-weight-bearing, ESR >40 mm/h, White cell count >12 × 10 9 /L]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
coreConcept: Hilton’s Law in Pediatric Hip Pain
front: Q: What physiological loop explains why pediatric hip pathology often presents as knee pain to parents?
back:
• Hilton’s Law: Joints are supplied by the same nerves as the muscles crossing them.
• Clinical Sign: Pain is referred from hip to knee via the obturator or femoral nerves.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 621 (Book Page): [Hilton’s law, which states that a joint is supplied by the same nerves as the muscles that move the joint, explains why many children present with knee pain although the pathology is in the hip.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What critical documentation must be shared with attendants upon emergency tourniquet application?
back:
• Precise application time recorded directly on the patient.
• Warning: Prolonged use causes irreversible limb ischemia.
• Requirement: Urgent surgical control is needed for safe reperfusion.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 376 (Book Page): [the length of time for which the tourniquet is applied must be recorded on the patient and the patient requires urgent surgical control of the bleeding in order to reperfuse the limb.]

category: Outline indications for urgent referral to orthopedic/trauma specialists
front: Q: What prehospital indicators trigger an immediate 'code red' trauma team activation upon hospital arrival?
back:
- Hemodynamic instability
- Acute airway compromise
- Requirement for massive transfusion protocols
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 375 (Book Page): Patients identifed before reaching hospital as being haemodynamically unstable or having acute airway compromise may initiate ‘code red’, triggering the automatic attendance of the most senior clinicians from each discipline.

category: Outline indications for urgent referral to orthopedic/trauma specialists
front: Q: What clinical finding in a supracondylar humeral fracture constitutes a surgical emergency for vascular referral?
back:
- A white, pulseless hand
- Requires immediate reduction and likely surgical exploration of the brachial artery
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 441 (Book Page): The white pulseless hand is a surgical emergency and requires immediate attention, assessment and urgent reduction.

category: Outline indications for urgent referral to orthopedic/trauma specialists
front: Q: What are the cardinal clinical indications for urgent referral and fasciotomy in suspected compartment syndrome?
back:
- Pain out of proportion to the injury
- Pain on passive stretch of the compartment muscles
- Tense, swollen limb (though clinical assessment of tension is unreliable)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): Compartment syndrome is a clinical diagnosis characterised by pain out of proportion, increasing pain, and pain on passive stretch... arrangements put in place to perform defnitive treatment with fasciotomies.

category: Outline indications for urgent referral to orthopedic/trauma specialists
front: Q: Why does a traumatic portal vein injury mandate urgent shunting and specialist center referral?
back:
- Primary ligation (tying off) carries a mortality rate exceeding 50%
- Requires specialist repair or shunting to ensure survival
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 401 (Book Page): Damage to the portal vein must be repaired, as tying of the portal vein carries a greater than 50% mortality rate. If it is not technically feasible to repair the vein at the time of surgery, it should be shunted and the patient referred to a specialist centre.

category: Outline indications for urgent referral to orthopedic/trauma specialists
front: Q: What are the primary objectives of urgent Damage Control Orthopaedic Surgery (DCO)?
back:
- Debridement of severe open fractures
- Temporary stabilization of long bone fractures
- Decompression of limb compartment syndrome
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 379 (Book Page): Damage control orthopaedic surgery is limited to debridement of severe open fractures, rapid temporary splint - age or stabilisation of long bone fractures and decompression of limb compartment syndrome where required.

category: Outline indications for urgent referral to orthopedic/trauma specialists
front: Q: What is the absolute clinical indication for urgent surgical decompression in spinal trauma?
back: - Deteriorating neurological function despite initial stabilization
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 416 (Book Page): The only absolute indication for surgery in spinal trauma is deteriorating neurological function.

category: Outline indications for urgent referral to orthopedic/trauma specialists
front: Q: When is urgent orthopedic referral indicated for a patient with a pelvic fracture in the emergency department?
back:
- Hemodynamic instability following blunt trauma
- Suspected 'open book' fracture requiring immediate compression binder and definitive stabilization
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 405 (Book Page): Severe pelvic injuries require a multidisciplinary team approach. If adequate orthopaedic experience is unavailable, consideration should be given towards early transfer of this patient to an institution with the necessary expertise.

category: Outline indications for urgent referral to orthopedic/trauma specialists
front: Q: Which ocular findings mandate emergency surgical referral for lateral canthotomy to prevent permanent blindness?
back:
- Tense proptosis
- Decreased visual acuity
- Loss of pupillary response (Retrobulbar hemorrhage)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 434 (Book Page): A retrobulbar haemorrhage is an acute surgical emergency as it can lead to blindness... preparation should be made for immediate bedside lateral canthotomy and cantholysis.

category: Outline indications for urgent referral to orthopedic/trauma specialists
front: Q: What are the urgent indications for surgical intervention in pediatric orbital 'white eye' blow-out fractures?
back:
- Oculocardiac reflex (bradycardia, nausea, syncope)
- Entrapment of the inferior rectus muscle causing potential muscle necrosis
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 413 (Book Page): Inferior rectus muscle entrapment in children may present as the oculocardiac refex: a triad of bradycardia, nausea and syncope. This needs to be treated as an emergency because irreversible damage related to muscle necrosis can occur within hours.

category: Outline indications for urgent referral to orthopedic/trauma specialists
front: Q: Which specific fracture characteristics mandate urgent transfer to a neurosurgical unit for possible evacuation?
back:
- Extradural hematoma with a 'talk and die' clinical pattern
- Lentiform (biconvex) hyperdense lesion on CT
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 386 (Book Page): Signifcant extradural haematoma mandates urgent transfer to the most accessible neurosurgical facility for immediate evacuation in deteriorating or comatose patients.

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What symptoms must attendants monitor for after discharge for a minor head injury?
back:
Seek immediate medical attention if the patient develops:
- Persistent/worsening headache or vomiting.
- Drowsiness or visual disturbances.
- Limb weakness or numbness.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 383 (Book Page): [Verbal and written head injury advice: seek medical attention if: Persistent/worsening headache despite analgesia, Persistent vomiting, Drowsiness, Visual disturbance, Limb weakness or numbness]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What basic care is required for a 'pink pulseless hand' after a pediatric supracondylar fracture?
back:
- Monitor closely for compartment syndrome symptoms.
- Maintain satisfactory perfusion and neurovascular checks.
- Pulse often returns within 24–48 hours following stabilization.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 463 (Book Page): [satisfactory perfusion of the limb, no suggestion of compartment syndrome and no neurological injury, then reduction and stabilisation of the fracture is warranted... Often the pulse will return within 24–48 hours.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: How do attendants distinguish cast tightness from the complication of compartment syndrome?
back:
- Compartment syndrome: Pain out of proportion and pain on passive stretch.
- Cast tightness: Relieved by limb elevation and splitting the cast to the skin.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [compartment syndrome is a clinical diagnosis characterised by pain out of proportion, increasing pain, and pain on passive stretch... Emergency treatment involves splitting casts and/or dressings to the skin]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Why is it explained to attendants that open fractures require delayed closure?
back:
- Allows radical debridement of contaminated or non-vital tissue.
- Prevents chronic deep infection (osteomyelitis).
- Ensures bone defects are managed before skin closure.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [Thorough debridement of any contaminated or non-vital soft tissue is important. Any loose or devitalised bone fragments should be discarded. Bone defects are easier to deal with than an infected non-union.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What is the long-term follow-up requirement for a child after Ponseti club foot correction?
back:
- Foot abduction orthosis (FAO) full-time for 3 months.
- Continued FAO use during nights and naps until age 4.
- Prevents high risk of deformity relapse.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 626 (Book Page): [The FAO is worn full time for 3 months and at ‘night and nap time’ for up to 4 years. Poor compliance with the FAO is associated with a higher relapse rate.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What clinical signs must attendants recognize in a 'talk and die' extradural haematoma?
back:
- Brief loss of consciousness followed by a 'lucid interval.'
- Sudden deterioration with contralateral hemiparesis.
- Ipsilateral pupillary dilatation (fixed and dilated).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 386 (Book Page): [Transient loss of consciousness is typical, and the patient may then present in the subsequent lucid interval with headache... There is contralateral hemiparesis, a reduced conscious level and ipsilateral pupillary dilatation]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Why is prolonged care on a spinal board contraindicated in trauma patients?
back:
- Causes rapid skin breakdown and pressure sores in insensate patients.
- Significant discomfort for patients with intact sensation.
- Usage must be restricted strictly to patient transfer.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 390 (Book Page): [Spinal boards lead to skin breakdown in insensate patients, and are very uncomfortable for those with normal sensation... They should only be used for transferring patients.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What long-term complications result from failing to follow-up on recurrent ACL instability?
back:
- High risk of secondary meniscal tears.
- Progressive articular cartilage degeneration.
- Early-onset osteoarthritis and functional disability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 504 (Book Page): [attempting subsequent cutting and pivoting activities, which can lead to recurrent instability... decrease the potential for further meniscal or articular cartilage degeneration.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What daily care routine prevents limb loss in diabetic foot patients?
back:
- Optimal glycaemic control and absolute smoking cessation.
- Daily inspection for ulcers or pressure areas.
- Use of professional-fitted footwear to relieve focal pressure.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 607 (Book Page): [optimising glycaemic control, improving vascular supply and relieving pressure, with appropriate footwear, much more important. This approach may avoid more extensive tissue loss or later amputation.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Why is a pediatric 'white eye' blowout fracture considered a surgical emergency?
back:
- Indicates inferior rectus muscle entrapment (oculocardiac reflex).
- Presents with bradycardia, nausea, and syncope.
- Causes irreversible muscle necrosis within hours.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 515 (Book Page): [This needs to be treated as an emergency because irreversible damage related to muscle necrosis can occur within hours... they are also described as a ‘white eye’ blowout fracture]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What warning signs should attendants watch for in a head-injured patient after hospital discharge?
back:
- Persistent or worsening headache
- Persistent vomiting
- Unusual drowsiness
- Visual disturbances
- Limb weakness or numbness
- If these occur, seek medical attention immediately.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 383 (Book Page): [Verbal and written head injury advice: seek medical attention if: Persistent/worsening headache despite analgesia; Persistent vomiting; Drowsiness; Visual disturbance; Limb weakness or numbness.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: How do the individual straps of a Pavlik harness function to stabilize a child's hip?
back:
- Anterior straps: Maintain hip flexion.
- Posterior straps: Limit adduction and promote abduction.
- This maintains the femoral head in the socket to allow acetabular remodeling.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 618 (Book Page): [The anterior strap of the Pavlik harness controls hip fexion, whereas the posterior strap limits adduction and encourages abduction.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Differentiate between 'real' and 'apparent' leg length discrepancy during patient education.
back:
- Real LLD: Actual physical difference in bone lengths.
- Apparent LLD: Leg looks short because of pelvic tilt or fixed deformity.
- Management differs based on the underlying cause.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 489 (Book Page): [LLD can be caused by a real diference in the leg lengths (the bones are diferent lengths) or by a deformity that makes the leg appear short because the pelvis must be tilted to get the leg onto the ground... the second is called ‘apparent’ LLD.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What clinical signs of early compartment syndrome must be reported immediately by attendants?
back:
- Pain out of proportion to the injury severity
- Increasing pain despite analgesics
- Intense pain on passive stretching of fingers or toes
- New onset numbness or tingling.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [Compartment syndrome is a clinical diagnosis characterised by pain out of proportion, increasing pain, and pain on passive stretch, with paraesthesia possible.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Why is tetanus status verification a critical basic care step in managing open fractures?
back:
- Open fractures are contaminated wounds communicating with the environment.
- Tetanus spores can enter via the skin breach.
- Prophylaxis is mandatory for patient safety and infection prevention.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [Any fracture with an overlying wound should be considered an open fracture... Obtain a tetanus immunisation history and treat accordingly.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Based on Ottawa rules, when should a patient with an ankle injury seek hospital imaging?
back:
- Inability to bear weight at the time of injury and during examination.
- Bone tenderness at the posterior 6cm of the lateral or medial malleolus.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 505 (Book Page): [Ottawa ankle rules. Bone tenderness along the distal 6 cm of the posterior margin or at the tip of the lateral malleolus... Inability to bear weight at the time of the accident or at the time of examination.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What is the long-term wear protocol for a Foot Abduction Orthosis (FAO) in clubfoot care?
back:
- Full-time wear (23 hours daily) for the first 3 months.
- Night and nap wear until approximately age 4 years.
- Strict compliance is essential to prevent deformity relapse.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 626 (Book Page): [The FAO is worn full time for 3 months and at ‘night and nap time’ for up to 4 years. Poor compliance with the FAO is associated with a higher relapse rate.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: Why is an 'unstable' Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE) considered a surgical emergency?
back:
- Defined by an inability to bear weight on the affected limb.
- It is equivalent to a displaced hip fracture.
- High risk of permanent avascular necrosis (AVN) if not treated promptly.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 622 (Book Page): [An unstable slip is defned by Loder as one in which the patient cannot bear weight... This situation is equivalent to a displaced intracapsular femoral neck fracture... The AVN risk is considerable.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: How do bisphosphonates improve quality of life for children with Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI)?
back:
- Decreases bone resorption and turnover.
- Clinically reduces bone pain and fracture frequency.
- Promotes weight-bearing mobility and improves overall bone strength.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 615 (Book Page): [Cyclical bisphosphonate treatment decreases bone resorption and turnover. This reduces bone pain and the fracture rate, promoting weight-bearing mobility and bone strength.]

category: Educate patients and attendants regarding basic care, need for follow-up, and complications
front: Q: What sensory area should patients monitor for complications after a shoulder dislocation?
back:
- The 'regimental badge area' (upper lateral arm).
- Numbness indicates axillary nerve injury.
- Important for documenting neurovascular complications post-reduction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 485 (Book Page): [Test sensation in the upper part of the lateral aspect of the arm (‘regimental badge area’)... Loss may indicate damage to the axillary nerve (following shoulder dislocation).]
